label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Ski cut 40 degree gully feature on NW Aspect that produced a Sz 2 Avalanche running approx. 200m.  Failure was on at ground.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Decent skinning and skiing. Be aware of sharks most places but overall good to be out to start the season.

reports.title: Bow Falls Wind Slab
reports.comment: quick: Slope fractured just above me as I was working my way up a 15 meter pocket of snow on lead. Entire slope slid 3 inches but did not continue due to rock barrier at bottom of the snow pocket.

reports.title: Obs Sub peak Nov6
reports.comment: quick: Rode the open tree shoulder slopes. surface snow was soft and light, boots penetrating 30-40cm and to ground. Unsupportive crusts buried 10cm or so but soft new snow, can be found

reports.title: Obs Sub Peak Nov 6
reports.comment: quick: HS 45cm average, immediate lees held 50-70cm. Rode the open tree shoulder slopes. surface snow was soft and light, boots penetrating 30-40cm and to ground. Unsupportive crusts buried 10cm or so buried by soft new snow, can be found sporadicly on South West slopes. Surface hoar was present BTL (2200m valley bottom) but was not found at the tree line (SW slopes 2300m). Snow surface was heavil…

reports.title: Roadside Bowl
reports.comment: quick: 15-20cm low density HST skied well. HS avg around 40-60cm in Alp. Pencil hard layer down ~30cm provided supportive skiing.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment:
avalanche: We saw two fresh sz 1 loose-dry. Triggered at the cliffs on the SW aspect of Obs Subpeak Bowl (the gully SE of the peak). 

The same aspect had the smooth "pillowy" look of wind deposits and the gully bottom had a large wind lip pointing SW. My rookie guess is we're getting windloading of this feature by winds from the NE / weather: Strong winds blowing NE across the ridge to the main s…

reports.title: Observation Sub-P
reports.comment:
avalanche: We saw two fresh sz 1 loose-dry. Triggered at cliff bands on the SW aspect above the Observation Subpeak bowl (the gully located SE from peak, where I've dropped this pin)

The same aspect had the smooth "pillowy" look of wind deposits and the gully bottom had a large wind lip pointing SW. My rookie guess is we're getting windloading by winds from the NE / weather: Strong winds blowing …

reports.title: Bow Summit Test Pit
reports.comment:
quick: Skiing quality was good, but new storm snow is consolidating and the powder is becoming heavier. Avoided areas with obvious wind affect. Dug a test pit out of curiosity. Results as follows:

Elevation: 2400m
Aspect: NE
Snow Depth: 105cm
Angle: 31 degrees
Air Temp: -4.5 Celsius
Results: No reaction in test pit. When the test column was pulled by hand afterwards, no layer sheered - the entire…

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment: quick: Fairly good skiing in areas on Observation subpeak. Fresh powder on a semi supportive rain crust below 2500m. Mix of wind affected snow with shallow/deep areas above that. We dropped a fairly large cornice along the summit ridge falling onto the E lee aspect and it popped a small wind slab about 20cm thick but did not run far at all given the mass of the cornice, we were surprised by the la…

reports.title: Cirque Sub Peak
reports.comment:
quick: A warm day for the Rockies. -10 and cold this morning but by mid day we found moist snow on steep South Asp in the Alpine.

Average snow depth was 50-70cm. Some great skiing was had but still shallow and rocky in general. 

Most of the slopes around Bow Summit have seen significant skier traffic.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Rode Jimmy Jr Bowl as an alternative to Bow resort. Conditions were very stable; dug a pit for fun with zero results. Not the freshest snow but soft enough where you could find fresh turns. Surprisingly good coverage, not a single shark was hit by any member of our party. Track out via the drainage is a bit of a luge run and thin in spots.

reports.title: Mount Jimmy Jr.
reports.comment: quick: For the most part the snow was very soft and stable. There was a bit of a weak layer forming on the west aspect covered with a thin layer (3-5) cm of fresh snow, where minor sluffing occurred on steeper slopes and concavities. It shouldn't be causing major problems in the future but something to keep in mind. No visible avalanches. The  uppermost portion of the mountain was still quite rock…

reports.title: Observation
reports.comment: quick: Skied two laps on Observation Peak, looker's left of Bow Pass in the slight tree triangle feature below the false summit. Went to high treeline/low alpine and found only 50cm HS. Oct crust was 3-4cm off ground with wet facets under it. Nov crust was 10-15cm below powder surface snow. Between we found a supportive mid pack of what I think was rounding facets (did not have snow study stuff to…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Found a 20cm dense wind slab in South Shoulder Chute (aka: Corner Chute, The Dog Leg, etc - lookers left of Stem Couloir) and non-wind affected powder snow at treeline all the way to the valley bottom. The wind slab was non-reactive, it was slightly cooler today and I'm assuming that helped keep it still. Snow depths are still variable in the area but the commonly skied runs have seen a lot…

reports.title: Observation
reports.comment:
quick: Did some snow pit work in the low alpine and skied a couple of laps down into treeline. Snowpack is highly variable for depth, two separate full profile pits had a difference of 30cm for HS and as you skinned around you could get down to 20cm in places. I would say the average is around 50cm for HS, with the deeper areas *maybe* getting close to 100cm.

We had sudden collapse failures on bo…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skinned to Helen Shoulder and dug a pit. 75cm HS in a lee area. HS is crazy variable in the area right now thanks to wind and sun. There was a dense wind slab in the upper snowpack that failed on medium compression test taps on every column. We did not see results on the Nov 8 crust which is 2-3cm thick. We got an easy result on one compression test on ground, the lower facets here were dry…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Skied the North facing sparse trees off of Crowfoot Glades.  Bow lake was frozen but wet in spots. There is still some open water around creeks and in the middle of the lake.  There was lots of snow but skiing was very poor skiers left, everything was wind hammered and facets in the sparse trees.  We decide not to ski the open bowl skiers hard left because it it was hallow sounding wind sla…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Wind affected snow at tree line and above. Surrounding peaks clearly had been scoured by the winds Thursday in their alpine zones. Surface stiffening in open zones from wind. Good snow quality of old powder/wind deposited snow at lower elevations in the trees.

reports.title: AST1 - Cloud Nine Guides - Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Hey All, 

Cloud Nine was out for its first AST1 of the season at Bow Summit Last weekend. Thought we’d pass on some conditions. First day out on skis, so took it pretty easy, focusing on trying to calibrate and gather a good density of observations.

Stormy day with ~20cm HN, and consistent west wind at 25km/hr gusting to 40. Lots of (snow) transport all day. Overcast and temps -2 cooling …

reports.title: Crowfoot roadside chutes
reports.comment: quick: Skied a few laps of the Crowfoot glades roadside chutes on Sunday. We stayed out of the alpine, and stuck to sheltered slopes at TL and below. We found approx. 25cms of new storm snow overlying various old crusts. The new snow remained low density in sheltered areas at TL and below. In snowpack tests, new snow produced occasional planar results on previous crust layer, but did not show sign…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Approximately 30 to 40 cms of new snow in Jimmy Jr bowl today. Mostly supportive crust underneath. Skied the trees on lookers left. Fantastic new snow quality, but the base is still a bit lacking with some lurking sharks. No wind effect in the trees.

Up higher in the bowl there was more noticable wind effect on the new snow. Still fantastic ski quality but less deep than in the trees. Lots…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder Burn
reports.comment:
snowpack: Skied on the burn area on Helen Shoulder.  About 15-20cm of fresh powder, though snow depth was variable and there were open creek crossings on the approach.  The wind was kicking up snow tornadoes at parkway level and peeling snow off the ridges, but significantly less wind in the burn.
  
Dug a quick pit about half way up the burn.   50-60 cm with 15-20cm of storm snow sitting on a thi…

reports.title: Bow Hut Weekend
reports.comment: quick: Bow Lake is not trustworthy yet, we took it wide without issue but don't go up the middle yet. Coverage in the approach canyon is acceptable after the storm. Lots of fresh snow in the area for Sunday - approx 30cm. The wind was also blowing. Tons of snow transport. We skied the toe of the glacier on both Saturday and Sunday and there was a significant difference in the amount of snow on Sun…

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Great short run in the trees off Helen shoulder today. Lots of coverage outside of the wind affected slopes.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: ~20 cm overnight dry powder with good stability. Warm temps just below zero with strong wind gusts observed during the day. Resulting in some tree bombs.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Took the direct south ridge up Dolomite Shoulder (don't bother with this variation right now, low snow, rock climbing and 1 tree climb) and skied back down the regular route. Snow in the area is amazing but there is no base, you must be careful not to hit rocks - there are hints of a crust but doesn't seem widespread enough to rely on to keep the coreshots at bay. We skied the first east fa…

reports.title: Mt Weed
reports.comment: quick: We skied off the summit of Mt Weed yesterday. An awesome line that we've been looking at for quite a while now. The approach was the crux. There was poor coverage until treeline. We bootpacked about 250m of elevation gain because of that. Crampons needed! Once we hit treeline it was smooth sailing. Snow was variable in the couloir, bit of everything from isolated wind slabs, sun crust, face…

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the Crowfoot Couloir today in fun condition! Soft skiing with a supportive enough crust to make bootpacking easy in the middle. Some faceting near the upper cliff band made for some inefficient last few meters. No signs of instability were noted, although there was wind affect on the fans, however soft turns were still found!
See snowpack tab for further details. / snowpack: The first…

reports.title: Observation Old Road Gully
reports.comment: quick: We skied a single lap on the false summit of Observation from about 2500m. We started in a small chute feature but moved out of it and directly into the "old road gully" main draw after finding a denser wind slab as we headed into a steeper convex roll section. We then skied around the upper waterfall choke and through the second choke where the snow improved greatly for turns. The ski down…

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Just barely enough snow to complete the Dolomite Circuit today. 10 good boot top pow turns down to Katherine Lake in a small wind loaded pocket was the highlight, but no base under it. Not much other good skiing was had. Not a lot of base in the area. Some rocks were ptexed. Great views this sunny bluebird day. We experienced a bit of the forecast inversion, but it did very little in the sh…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Awesome day in the Jimmy Jr bowl with about 12 other people (2-3 different groups lapping the bowl throughout the day). 
Also took a walk over to the main face of Jimmy Simpson and saw two groups. Soft snow on top of wind crust maybe 10 cm down.

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson Face
reports.comment:
weather: -20C at the car in the morning with steady warming throughout the day (not solar related, we spent the whole day in the shade).

Clear skies all day. 

No winds. / snowpack: Observed evidence of strong winds out of the NW (moving down the valley). Most NW aspects were scoured down to ground, and hard wind features just adjacent. The features were up to 30cm high. 

Did a few hasty pits as…

reports.title: Cirque fore-peak
reports.comment:
quick: Inversion today: -20C at num-ti-jah at 10am and maybe -5C in alpine. Slight north winds picking up later in afternoon. 

Snow was quite facetted below tree line and cold temperatures made it feel brittle like styrofoam. At and above treeline facetting was prevalent only in shallow and rocky areas. Alpine snowpack was variable due to wind effect with HS ranging from 40-80cm in most spots. Lo…

reports.title: Observation Roadside Drainage
reports.comment: quick: Skied the alpine area above the longer roadside drainage feature on Observation from about 2500m in a mix of supportive facets and isolated wind slab. Overall the skiing was ok and it was sunny and warm up high. Another party skied the same area after us but they dropped in from the higher bench area and skied the looker's left shoulder of the drainage where they looked to find better snow …

reports.title: Dolomite Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Very long approach to a nice bowl. Great snow in a little hidden and wind sheltered area near the small couloir on dolomite. Thanks Jeff and Clem!

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: Pretty mellow noticed spin drifts and stuff coming from higher more wind affected slopes

reports.title: Bow summit - South shoulder tree chutes
reports.comment: quick: Skied many laps of below-the-knee deep powder today on the South shoulder tree chutes. Face shots and fun times. Moved further south on the apron once there were about 12 skiers in the area and did a single run to road toward Jimmy jr. bowl. Powder was substantial on apron that travel downhill was slow and difficult.   Expected high sloughs from Lookers right of flower couloir observed, but…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Observed Shooting cracks at treeline.  
S2 all day.

reports.title: Cirque Sub-Peak
reports.comment:
quick: We stayed away from lee slopes.
Moderate westerlies were transporting snow at ridgetop on Mts Temple, Olive, Gordon, Crowfoot.

On drive home we observed numerous Sz 1-1.5 slab avalanches on lee loaded alpine slopes along Mt Crowfoot. / avalanche: East face of Mt Jimmy Simpson
Large slab in centre gully running into tree line trees.

reports.title: Helen shoulder Sitting Bull
reports.comment: quick: Rode sitting bull today, 50-70cm HS with lots of thin spots.  Expect to hit a shark or two although the skiing is generally quite good.  Sun was on the slope all day today, we had lunch without gloves and toques but did not get a temp reading.  No cohesive slab noted in the bowl.  Lookers right of sitting bull had some soft wind/storm slab although the bowl appeared sheltered. No whumpfing,…

reports.title: West Nile Glades
reports.comment: quick: Deep trail breaking uphill and skiing downhill, audible remote avalanches and shedding on steep unskiable terrain in alpine up to size 2.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Rode the crowfoot glades. Snow was waist deep at times. Observed two crowns from slides above the glades that must have happened last night. Some sloughing off the cliffs as well.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: New snow layer seems to be settling quickly with the warm temps but provided some amazing riding quality. Coverage in the trees was good. / weather: -4 @ 11am at car, 0 at car on return. 

Cloudy to clearing slightly, low cieling

Small granular snow falling on arrival. Disipated quickly

Trees sloughing from warmth. / snowpack: 2200m Elevation 30° slope
HST 80cm
CTM11 sudden planar at 45cm…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: We stayed in the tree line and kept it conservative. Observed some natural 2-2.5 slab and loose snow avalanches near observation peak. Observed wind slab as well.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak Glades
reports.comment: quick: Had a fun day in the glades. Only saw a few Small Point release avalanches on the steeper slopes with exposed rocks and a small collapsed cornice. Skiing was very supportive powder.

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Enjoyed a great day in the Jimmy Junior Bowl. Fresh powder an top of a supportive, but unreactive crust. There was a small slide on the far lookers right of the bowl when we got up there in the morning, but we enjoyed great stability during the day on the slopes we rode.

One of our party lost a ski and we were unable to find it. If anyone happens upon it please let me know at karljparkinso…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder Burn/Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Skiing was good in the Helen Shoulder burn and glades. Open slope at the burn showed no signs of instability and snow was floaty powder with a supportive crust underneath. The glades showed little sign of instability, however some whumpfs were observed when skiing, especially when punching through the crust lower down. However these were small localized settlements. Overall a good day out!
…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment:
snowpack: CTM/H (SP) @ 65

Similar results in the trees below

reports.title: OXO
reports.comment:
weather: -16C in the morning, -11C as the sun was going down (4:30pm). 

Recent winds must have been all over the place: saw evidence of winds out of NW and SW in the alpine, and from the SE at T.L.

No clouds all day. / snowpack: HS 5-60cm. Fresh unconsolidated snow down to ground. We all scraped our bases today.

reports.title: Bow Summit "south hump glades"
reports.comment: snowpack: Single compression test - Ground cover beneath snow: alpine heather species. Conditions Clear, light breeze, Minus 15 C

reports.title: Observation Glades
reports.comment: quick: Some whumpfing in isolated pockets but largely snow seemed stable. Dug a pit to look and found 25cms of powder on top of supportive wet base. This is an isolated pocket so I wouldn’t take it more than that. / avalanche: Saw 1 old slide and two new slides on the bowls below observation peak. Two were slabs for sure. One look like a point release but ran long. / snowpack: Did an ECT. No failu…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Skin tracks were well established but slope were not heavy skied. No signs of resent avalanches other than a little slough that had come off the head wall.

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Overall good skiing up little crowfoot peak. The glacier was particularly good. Wind effect varies in the area. No wumphing or recent avalanche activity of note.
Glacier coverage varied from 1.2-2.5m and there was lots of wind transport taking place in the zone throughout the day.

reports.title: Cirque SW side
reports.comment:
snowpack: Sw aspect at 2567m had a 120~ cm base, resistant planer failure 65cm down at ECTP#28. This was on a pencil hard layer.  We did several shovel compression tests with similar failures in the same location. 

Also noted inversion temps. -19 at the car at 10am, and down to base layers in the alpine with the sun shining. Otherwise fantastic skiing with beautiful powder and good company.

reports.title: Crowfoot glacier
reports.comment:
avalanche: Poor visibility from our vantage point, size is unconfirmed. Audible avalanche from 500m away, we saw debris flowing off the Crowfoot Glacier near Crowfoot Falls. 

Frequent size 1 loose dry avalanches out of the headwall with new snow and wind. 

Several size 1.5 windslab avalanches on NE moraine features that are likely a week old.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Rode Crowfoot Glades with at least three other parties this morning. Snow was amazing and there were no signs of instability or wind effect on any aspects that we saw. We did see some sluff coming off the cliffs above us. The Bow isn't fully frozen and there are a few thin spots but crossing is easy enough.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Lots of new snow in the Bow Summit area but sounds like less than to the south-east (sunshine/93s). Some moderate wind for a short time mid day, otherwise low winds while we were out. Steady snowfall in the area all day. Limited obs due to cloud cover.

The road has 30-40cm of snow on it and was down to a single lane for sections. Driving outside of the packed "trail" was difficult, high cl…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Bow Summit - did 4 laps at Bow Summit today. Stuck to treeline slopes up to low 30 degree range. 30-45cm of settled storm snow sits on a ~10cm thick firmer layer that separates the storm snow from the facet bed beneath. Trail breaking wasn't as difficult as expected because of this layer - ski pen being about 20cm, but boot pen was VERY deep. Had to transition on 1 ski. Ski quality was gene…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder burnt trees
reports.comment:
quick: Skied 2 laps on the Helen Shoulder burned trees and had surprisingly good conditions and turns.

Dug a pit at 2223m S185 direction and 26 degree slope angle. 
Two columns 1m apart had a bit of a different 0-30cm make up. No result on the 109cm column, CT27 on the other down 60cm on the 5cm thick facet layer above the crust. 

Based on this we kept skinning up and skied a 25ish degree slope …

reports.title: Bow Hut + Onion
reports.comment: quick: Went into Bow Hut on the 26th for a night. Extremely cold start at -30, warming to -10 in the alpine. Entire route including the approach canyon is covered very well now. The head-wall chute is covered in avy debris from the storm, so it's not very sketchy anymore. Snow almost everywhere was generally wind affected, and mostly didn't ski well besides some isolated pockets. Some drumming sou…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Got a few whumpfs on the skin track and one person in our group got a settlement and shooting cracks when going over a slight convex roll. Solar aspects in the afternoon had visual slumping. Surface hoar was present. Several older avalanches higher up on the lee side of the shoulder, see attached photo

reports.title: Bow Summit Road Side
reports.comment: quick: Bow Summit has been hit pretty hard since the last storm. Most of the simple terrian was chewed up.  Expect to ski lines with overhead risk if you want fresh turns. Ski quality was very good. Surface hoar was forming.

reports.title: Crowfoot chutes and pillows
reports.comment: quick: Amazing day at Crowfoot skiing chutes and pillow lines. Up track sucked - especially given somebody had the bright idea to try their snowshoes in the skin track ... aside from that unpleasantness, amazing boot top facets to ski down chutes and pillow lines over a supportive mid pack and garbage underneath. No signs of instabilities throughout the day and still really good lines to be skied …

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Stuck within tree line and took a mellow line down. Only did one lap due to weather conditions. Snow was good to ski, great coverage and deep. On return, skin track across the lake was nearly covered - blowing wind increased from morning to afternoon. Dug a pit - total snow 165cm, weak facet layer was present about 130cm down (35cm from ground).

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Surface hoar present down 60cm as expected below treeline, even in some wind exposed open areas. Weak facet near ground.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment:
quick: Busy day at crowfoot with 10+ cars at 10am. Storm provided 30-40 cm of fresh with intense winds increasing in afternoon. Lots of weather activity, numerous cornice falls and spindrift all day off the headwall above and size 1-2 off next large fan north, lakeside. 

We popped one 0.5 in mellow terrain on a small convexity, which would have had some consequence had it been closer to the centr…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: We rode the Crowfoot Chutes area today, accessed by the main ridge skin track. Winds were light all day, and accompanied by light snowfall (1-2cm). We conducted Multiple hand shear tests on a convex roll which failed instantly when isolating the columns. We also observed numerous shooting cracks on steep pillow features. We did a compression test at 2150m on a west facing TL 20 deg slope. W…

reports.title: Crowfoot Christmas Party
reports.comment:
quick: Not much change from yesterday report, other then more tracks that weren’t filled in over nights No major wind effect from yesterday at top of bench, didn’t explore higher than 2210m. First and second exit chutes and terrain trap middle drainage were triggering the lizard brain and we stayed away. 

Far skiers left  off the bench is essentially tracked out and will need a refresh. Older tra…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Incredible riding quality at Crowfoot Glades. 30 to 40cm of fresh snow. We skied chutes #1 #2 and the tree triangle. Had some minor sloughing on steeper convex features on chute #2 (in trees).

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Rode chute 5 multille times.Minor sluffing occurred on the steeper entrance but observed no other signs of activity. Did witness a cornice dropping off crowfoot mountain. High winds in the late afternoon covered previous tracks upon exit.

reports.title: Grand Daddy
reports.comment: quick: Early morning observations around Now Peak provided evidences of a widespread natural cycle up to SZ 3 on all aspects in the last 48 hrs but most likely all from the the important wind event. Most larger avalanches had been triggered by large cornice falls, pulling deep slabs in features that had not previously avalanched and loose avalanches in couloir features. Grand Daddy had a very rece…

reports.title: Deep Persistent Slab - Bow Peak
reports.comment:
avalanche: Avalanche occurred between 1030 and 1430. At its deepest it appears to be ~2m deep. Cornice still intact along ridge. Several areas of the fan also slid to ground.

The Deep Persistent Slab is a problem that will linger for a long period and should always be on your mind.

reports.title: Deep Persistent Slab - Sub Observation
reports.comment:
avalanche: Wind loaded slope, failed at the ground on facets/depth hoar. 

The Deep Persistent Slab is a problem that will linger for a long period and should always be on your mind.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: avalanche: The avalanche was trigger by the party in front of us.  Nobody was involved in the incident.  S-SE facing slopes in this area appeared heavily wind loaded.  We observed another avalanche that seemed to be a couple days old on a similar aspect but slightly higher elevation and about a 25 degree slope.  Likely from severe wind loading.

reports.title: Hellen Burn Area
reports.comment:
quick: Temps -15C and partly cloudy, winds calm at 11am at the crowfoot pull out along 93N.  Temps warmed to -6 around noon, and dropped to -10 at ridge top.  Light ESE wind likely signalling the arctic air coming in around 1pm with a trend to cloudier conditions.  Temps dropping slightly to -12C around 4pm, mostly cloudy and light snow (<1cm).

BTL Snowpack depth varied from 90 to 150 cm dependin…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Observed a couple small slides on steeper, north facing slopes and a small (0.5) skier triggered on convex feature.

reports.title: Observation peak
reports.comment: quick: Wind affected in many places above treeline. Compression test resulted a pop, 12 Medium at 45cm deep. Skied mellow slopes and the ski quality was okay. Didn't do a second lap because it was too cold.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: We skied the TL and BTL slopes south of the bow summit parking lot. We skied from 2100 to 2350m. Sky was overcast all day, snowing up to S1 when we left at 2:00pm. Winds were nill in the morning, increasing to mod from the NW in the afternoon, with obvious snow transport. Temps were -24 in the morning. We saw approx 2 cms of new snow through the day. 

We saw one Sz 0.5 skier triggered wsl …

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: avalanche: 10-15cm of snow in 24hrs at Bow Summit during a warming period (-25 to -8). Avalanche initiated out of the steep rocky terrain and pulled a persistent slab on the open slope below.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Nice riding in the glades today! Temps stayed around -5 all afternoon, calm wind. Dug a pit at 2210m NE aspect on a 30 degree slope, HS 210cm. CTH 24 non-planar break 60cm down. Saw 3 instances of natural sloughing off Crowfoot Mountain above.

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Crossed the West side of Dolomite slopes early in the morning to avoid warming.  There was evidence of debris in the slide path tracks, but it was not recent.  Saw pin wheels releasing from shallow rocks on upper south west slopes in the afternoon.  Evidence of significant wind transport, forming a large cornice on South side of Cirque Peak.  On the back (north east) Dolomite Peak, observed…

reports.title: Mosquito Creek
reports.comment: snowpack: CTM Q1 Sudden Planar on BSH down 55cm SW aspect.  See more: IG @anchorage_avalanche_center

reports.title: Grandaddy couloir
reports.comment: avalanche: Three triggered at feet on descent of GDaddy couloir in areas where snow had not been flushed out naturally by recent cornice fall. / snowpack: ECTP29, CTM14 both Q1 sudden planar.

reports.title: Low Angle Slopes on Observation Peak
reports.comment: quick: Fun day skiing low angled slopes on observation peak. Snow at and below treeline was fantastic, started to thin and feel a bit hollow above. Mild temperatures (-11 to -2C) with about 10cm on new snow over a supportive base.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Skiing was excellent. Several persons doing laps in the burn reported good skiing. We stuck to the ridge and trees. / weather: Very light snow falling most of the day. / snowpack: No failure on our our one test = CTH NR
There is a layer about 95 cm down that fails with a solid hip check.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Good skiing at Jimmy jr bowl, with about 10 cm of fresh snow on a supportive crust.

Noticed many sluffs in steep alpine terrain on walls of bowl, but no movement when skiing.

reports.title: Bow Peak
reports.comment:
weather: AM: -5C, 8/8 clouds
PM: 0C, 3/8 clouds

Moderate winds in the alpine but not sustained. Direction was towards Crowfoot Pass (N winds arriving at the pass, S winds while we ascended the summit) / snowpack: Ventured into the alpine to summit Bow Peak via SW face. No pit, but I was pole-probing and digging back every few meters.

Highly variable snowpack to say the least. Some spots had soft…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skinned up and over the highpoint of Dolomite Shoulder and took a walk along the ridge/sub peaks before heading back and skiing the shoulder run. Amazing powder snow conditions from the high knob all the way back to the road. Snow was not deep but skied wonderfully. Two members of our group skied the last larger bowl feature before getting to treeline and reported great snow, I skied along …

reports.title: Crowfoot glades and chutes
reports.comment:
quick: No rain crust was found on the appriach at valley bottom. 
10 cm of light snow over about 20-30 cm of denser snow on the old uptrack. 
Saw Na sz 1 on the steep slope below cliffs from yesterday, scraped to ground but didn't run far  (see pic).
No NA activity was heard today except of one small sluff observed from steep terrain. Vis was mostly poor. 
Crowfoot couloir had derby close to the b…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: avalanche: 50m above our location on open talus. Surprisingly thin snowpack (80cm), 160cm to 2m below. / snowpack: Surface Hoar down 75cm. 15cm depth hoar at bottom.

reports.title: Dolomite circuit
reports.comment: avalanche: We skied the Dolomite today - the very 1st avie path you cross (maybe 20 minutes from road) going clockwise just over the ridge from the parking lot down to the stream has slid a few days ago. What is notable is that it was  full path, taking out the trees that used to frame that short downhill to the creek.  In my 30 years of skiing that route at least once a year, I have never seen th…

reports.title: crow foot glades chutes
reports.comment:
quick: We road the wide open roadside chute. Observed cross loading from north west winds blowing up the chute at the top. 3 cm wind crust on top of powder at the entrance and good quality powder down below. The winds were really strong at times even in the trees walking up the skin track.
 Heard an avalanche come down somewhere close but could not see it, also observed a old size 1 avalanche unde…

reports.title: Observation Sub-Peak, South / East Slopes
reports.comment: quick: Wind was transporting snow, stayed away from those areas.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Warm and sheltered day lapping West Nile Lookers left avy path. There were several other groups in the area but plenty of fresh remains. No avalanche activity or concerns noted.

reports.title: Bow Headwall Avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Intense winds overnight at bow hut starting around 0300 and still gusting throughout the the day. Flat/low light and low visibility near the hut all morning. / avalanche: Skier accidental trigger on Headwall coming out of Bow hut. Skier was partially buried and able to self extricate. No injuries. Shooting cracks and whumpfing   observed on all snow near and below the hut/cirque and observe…

reports.title: Mosquito Cr.
reports.comment: quick: Long tour today into low angle trees for a few turns. Snow was very crusty right at the trail head. Soft again, once up a bit higher. / avalanche: Did not run far, only in the slope it started into.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr bowl
reports.comment: quick: JJ Bowl offered boot deep powder skiing from top to bottom today. Wind activity above us had frequent snow skiffs and a few small sloughs come over the top, mostly in the northern hanging bowl but not continuing into the main bowl.  No stability concerns noted today.

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit beginning
reports.comment:
avalanche: We skied the Dolomite today - the very 1st avie path you cross (maybe 20 minutes from road) 
going clockwise just over the ridge from the parking lot down to the stream has slid a few days ago. 
What is notable is that it was full path, taking out the trees that used to frame that short downhill to the creek.
In my 30 years of skiing that route at least once a year, I have never seen th…

reports.title: Grand Daddy
reports.comment: incident: 3/4 of the way up, 2 guys washed out from overhead slide, tumbled 800m to the fan.

reports.title: Cirque Peak Natural avalanches
reports.comment: avalanche: We were on Helen Shoulder and observed these two size 1.5 natural avalanches.  They were not there around noon and then saw them around 13:30.  They came off the east aspect of the south ridge (climb route) on Cirque Peak.  There was a spike in westerly winds to 80ish KM/h early afternoon.  A couple times we had to engage 'the stance' to not get blown over.  We assume these winds were t…

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment: snowpack: Multiple pits dug(ast2 course). Mod and hard sudden collapse on facets and Depth hoar under nov. Crust in pit with 115 to 135cm snow. Pit with 70cm deoth=no result(all loose facets) pit with 300cm also no result.

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: quick: We opted to ski Flower Couloir on the 16th. Snow was very good, deep and soft. On the approach to the fan of the couloir we observed some variable wind affected snow. Nothing discouraging in regards to the line. As it was rather sheltered and very filled in. During the boot pack, there was a rather low energy wind skin 4cm deep in the snow pack, very close to the surface. We noticed it may …

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Lots of snow coming off BowCrow Peak some dissipating into the air, a few causing avalanches. Could not see where the slide patha ended. We stayed skiers right.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr bowl
reports.comment: quick: Conservative day going for leftover laps at Jimmy Jr. Bowl: compared to a week ago the snow was much denser and there was more wind effect noted even in this sheltered area. Old tracks from another party ?1-2 days ago were bulletproof (An old horizontal skin track across the bowl was actually a bit of a hazard as a result). Ski quality was good with mid boot powder and no slabby feel. Left …

reports.title: Bow Summit study plot profile
reports.comment: quick: Bow Summit study plot profile

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: No Whumpfing. Large cornices have developed overhead on the rock face. Large convex roller to navigate where the ridge trail (shoot access) meets the pillow line route on the way to the pass. We turned around at the convex roller due to terrain trap below. Other party went up in similar area, but got turned around near the pass due to large wind lip of some sort. 
Glades and first few shoot…

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Mixed bag today going up Little Crowfoot.  Our original objective was Crowfoot Mountain but we managed Little Crowfoot and the stoke was high considering. We had whiteout chaos some moments.  A lot of that new snow is moving...fast.  Wind slab formation in the alpine seemed instantaneous.  We noticed nothing active but it seemed lurking.  All that wind scour has to be depositing somewhere.

reports.title: Mosquito Creek
reports.comment: quick: Observed fracture on NNW face of Noseeum Peak

reports.title: Jimmy Jr bowl.
reports.comment: quick: Ascended the drainage to the bowl on firm packed trail.  HN 10-15 . Variable snow conditions ranging from fresh over layers to hard slab . Low light made the run interesting.   Sun out on 2nd run.  Light wind during the runs,  temp -11.   Sluffs coming off several aspects ,  point release triggered.

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Nice day for some hot laps. Snow stability was great, and consistent with the avalanche.ca condition reporting (good job as always). Ski tracks from the last week were covered over with about 10-15cm of new snow. At times you could still feel the old tracks underneath, but mostly it was nice pow skiing. There was also some chunder here and there from fallen cornices, and previous small aval…

reports.title: Patterson Center Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Good conditions on the Patterson couloirs on Sunday. Observed evidence of loose dry slough in the couloir and on adjacent steep/overhead terrain, probably from the snowfall/wind combo the day before. No avalanches observed on the terrain visible from the route. The top 20 m was wind effected and the snowpack degraded to 30-60 cm wind slab on facets. See "snowpack" for pit results at the top…

reports.title: Helen lake and shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up almost to Helen lake and then went back down on Helen shoulder. Sunny in the morning then the snow moved in about 1 pm. Poor visibility and light snow for the rest of the afternoon. 
Up towards Helen lake, snow was supportive and no signs of instability. We stayed away from convex slopes. Looked like lots of wind loading on opposite side of the valley (Dolomite). Skiing down the s…

reports.title: Grand Daddy
reports.comment: quick: Conditions were good, some small natural sluffing but nothing crazy. We at one point heard a rock or ice fall but when it cleared up and the clouds broke we were unable to see anything. The cornice above grand daddy is getting big. Watch out for that when the weather warms up. / weather: Below tree line had some wet snow once the clouds broke around 3pm

reports.title: Crowfoot Trees
reports.comment: quick: Significant avalanche activity witnessed off Crowfoot Mountain. Cornice failures as well as loose snow avalanches to size 2.5. 1/2 dozen or more witnesses during our outing 4-5 hours. / avalanche: Multiple avalanches were seen dropping off Crowfoot Peak. Several were large sized (to 2.5). Cornice failure witnessed. / weather: Light gusting winds to tree line, alpine appeared to have stronge…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up to Puzzle Peak ramp but it looked heavily wind effected from a distance so decided to go up Dolomite Shoulder instead. Wind effected snow above tree line made for compact skiing, but lots of powder to be found on S facing slopes between treeline and 2000m. Below 2000m we found less powder, sitting on a noticeable crust at ~10cm depth. 

Visibility was limited to the closest peaks …

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Our group toured up Crystal Ridge today. We dug multiple pits looking to assess conditions on the East side of the Parkway. 
We found sun crust on steep solar aspects up to 2250 meters. Snow at the tree line and in open areas is wind affected.
15-20 cms new snow. / weather: Lightly snowing all day, very fine snow. / snowpack: At 14:30 we dug a pit at tree line looking for windslab. 2400M, W…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: A great day out at West Nile. The day was mostly sunny and calm in the morning, with wind increasing noticeably into the afternoon. No new snow accumulation during the day. No signs of the dust-on-crust that was found below 2000m on the SW slopes of Dolomite Shoulder the day before. Snow conditions were ~20cm of light powder which fell within the previous 48hrs and was slightly wind affecte…

reports.title: Bow Summit - Upper Trees
reports.comment: quick: Propagated upslope of skier trigger point and then across the slope

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
avalanche: Sa triggered by 4th skier, propagated 10m uphill and up to 40m across; no involvement. Same layer failed CTM 12, 100m uphill same aspect.

Trigger point marked by "X" in picture.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: we were riding crowfoot glades at treeline, in a low risk terrain area as all debris was flowing down another path opposite side to the ridge
witnessed around 8 size 1 to 3's heard quite a lot in the distance from crowfoot mountain/glacier
this was my first backcountry experience having done my ast 1, went with experienced people. awesome powder

dug a pit on same slope angle as we were rid…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Snow was good! Lots of options and a few different party’s out there today sticking to the trees and some pillows. ￼￼ / avalanche: Lots of activity off the crowfoot mountain wall. We could hear larger sized slides somewhere in the glacier bowls but due to visibility we couldn’t see them. / weather: Snowing on and off from S1-S3, it was lightly filling in tracks the whole day. / snowpack: We…

reports.title: West Nile is Good
reports.comment:
quick: Great day at West nile. Some small loose dry sluffing was observed on convex rolls.

Snow ranged from boot top to knee deep in places. Observed sluffing off steep rock headwall above.

reports.title: Observation sub peak glades
reports.comment:
snowpack: 15cm of fresh light cold powder, No obvious layers in the new snow and seemed well bonded to older storm snow.

Some pockets of shallower snowpack near rocks/trees had sugary facets just below recent storm slab.

No evidence of rain crust under storm snow.

reports.title: Observation sub peak
reports.comment:
quick: Hand shear test had the new snow sliding on old surface layer 

One crack on steeper open slope otherwise snowpack seemed well bonded and no whumping or other cracks observed

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: A good day of skiing at West Nile. Loose-dry sluffing on steep slopes and convex rolls. Sun packed a punch and observed point-release sluffing in alpine / snowpack: Loose-dry sluffing on steep slopes. Warm afternoon temperatures were warming things up in the alpine and we observed lots of sluffing up high

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak West Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Awesome day to be out ski touring instead of TP shopping, and enjoyed the awesome views. 
Found a few turns in sheltered and mostly south facing lee slopes in tree line areas, but got more variable toward the alpine areas.
Alpine areas are wind hammered - fine for A-to-B travelling but not for turns. Wumpfing with radiating cracks in this area. / avalanche: No signs of recent avalanches see…

reports.title: Mosquito Mountain gladed shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Started in -23C at 11am leaving the car, rapid temperature rise around 12-1pm. Snow became heavy and wet on our way out around 2-3pm. Back at the car at 4:30pm car said temp was +1C.

Wind slabs on many aspects from valley bottom to protected areas in trees and open areas, varying from 0.5cm to 5cm. 

We skied up Mosquito Creek and up the gladed shoulder in front of Mosquito Mountain / towa…

reports.title: Wapta and Mt Thompson
reports.comment: quick: Wapta conditions & Mt Thompson - Mar 14, 15 2020. 3 of us went in to Peyto Hut and back via Bow Lake. Skied Mt Thompson on our way out. Widespread wind affect pretty typical for the Wapta, but in more places than usual due to the opposing winds during the week. Lots of wind slabs/ crusts, drumming, cracking, sastrugi, and crappy skiing to be found! Cold snow was slow and high friction until…

reports.title: Cirque fore peak glades
reports.comment: quick: Great day out in the sun. -30 in the parking lot then warmed up to near zero during the day. We have been waiting for a blue bird day like this all season long! We skied nice power in the trees and the snow just gets more wind affected as you move higher up. See snowpack tab for pit test results. / snowpack: We dug a pit at tree line and performed a CT. There was 20 cm of fist over finger d…

reports.title: Cirque Peak was busy !🎿
reports.comment: quick: Cirque Peak was a popular objective today given the amazing wx ! Started off from Num-Ti-Jah at -28’C at 9am. Counted something like 14 folks that came in from both Dolomite and Num-Ti-Jah that went down the N couloir onto the glacier. Social distancing was a challenge ! 😁 Alpine was quite wind affected everywhere. Rap into the couloir definitely is more than 30m - party before us were gene…

reports.title: Pow on Crystal Ridge!
reports.comment:
quick: Had an awesome day skiing the back side of crystal ridge today! The north facing slopes are still holding boot deep powder while the road side of crystal ridge was nice corn around 3 pm. 

We rode the slope beside sugar cube but could see some people dropped into sugar cube couloir probably yesterday. Lots of good turns to be had out there still! 

Should note that we cut off some soft wind…

reports.title: PAC-Man couloir
reports.comment:
quick: Rode PAC-Man couloir. March 18th 10ish am. 
Decent travel up the shoulder to cross the bowl below the couloir. Boot pack up the pac man was nice , crusty and good for the boot pack but enough to get an edge on the ride down , riding the bowl down to the lake was really good conditions with 5ish cm of snow on top of crust. Enjoy the pics !

reports.title: Mount Gordon/Wapta conditions
reports.comment: quick: Skied Mt Gordon from the road, up the Bow Hut approach. Overall coverage is good throughout, with very good bridging on the glacier. Very sunny, though the wind took the edge off; there was a hard crust varying from 5cm thick to greater covered by 5-10cm of new snow. On descent we noted several new wet and dry loose avalanches including in the canyon; likely triggered by solar input. / weat…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Got some good turns on the open slope skiers left of crowfoot glades. North facing aspects are still holding great powder on the icefields parkway although this one was pretty tracked out. No signs of instability. Keeping it mellow to avoid injury of course.

reports.title: Grand daddy
reports.comment: quick: Full crust recovery overnight with a 1-3cm K mfcr on all aspects. Sky overcast with a trace amount of new snow throughout the day. 10-15cm 4f on sheltered n asp @ tl and btl but tough to find in the alp. Crust present and wind effect in all open areas, even areas with minimal solar input. No significant na observed nor any significant old activity. One small sluff in the grand daddy but ove…

reports.title: Bow Summit - North Face
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing quality in the north facing bowl below Pac-Man Couloir, above Bow Summit. Thin on the edges, but the guts were very supportive with soft snow on top (where we skied). Skin track up was conservative up the ridge with a small boot pack near ridge top. Recent tracks in the couloir (~2 days). Lots of avalanches in steep alpine terrain on solar aspects; dry and slab. Another party th…

reports.title: Cornice failure
reports.comment:
avalanche: Observed Na sz1.5 cornice failure triggered dry loose above crowfoot glades at 15:45 temperature was -3c wind calm and light from N in pm 
Noticeable sun effect on upper snowpack , good skiing in the shade .

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment: quick: Idea travel conditions on the Dolomite Circuit. Later in the afternoon the snow about 200 metres above the Parkway soften up.

reports.title: Crowfoot Area
reports.comment:
quick: Stuck to non-solar aspects today. It was beautiful out, stayed away from other groups, parked secluded, and truly social distanced door to door. 
Skiing was quite good in the shade, we skied chutes/pillow terrain. Test pit at TL showed stability in the upper and mid pack. At 1600hrs we observed from afar, avalanche off of Crowfoot Mountain North peak (the usual spot) cornice failure, loose …

reports.title: Puzzle peak
reports.comment: quick: Terrible sun crust. Only softened up at lower elevations. Noticed some old sluff coming off of cliffs in surrounding areas that were in the sun. Poor ski quality good day to stretch the legs.

reports.title: West Nile/Grandaddy
reports.comment: quick: Went skiing in the west nile area, planning to look at grand daddy. Turned around before fan due to poor visibility, strong snowfall and strong wind. Alpine beginning to develop wind slabs, skiing in the slide path below treeline was quite good until lower down. Snow started somewhat wet at about 6am and become dryer throughout the morning.

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: Skied bow summit today. The parking lot was dead quite only 2 other cars. The snow was pretty good and the clouds opened up and revealed the sun as we climbed and only came back out when we got back to the car around 3:00. We got to the top ridge of the front face and had decent turns down in powder with small areas with debris or chunks. There was a crust below the new snow but riding qual…
